```python
# test_is_balanced_parens.py
import pytest

from your_module import is_balanced_parens  # replace with the actual module name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "s",
    [
        "",
        "()",
        "[]",
        "{}",
        "()[]{}",
        "{[()]}",
        "({[]})",
        "{[()()]()}",
        "text with no brackets",
        "a(b[c]{d}e)f",
        "fn(a[0]) { return b; }",
        "{ [ ( ) ] }",
    ],
)
def test_balanced_inputs_return_true(s):
    assert is_balanced_parens(s) is True


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "s",
    [
        "(",
        "[",
        "{",
        ")",
        "]",
        "}",
        "(]",
        "[)",
        "{]",
        "([)]",
        "{[(])}",
        "((())",
        "())",
        "}{",
        "abc(def",
        "abc)def",
        "([{}]))",
    ],
)
def test_unbalanced_inputs_return_false(s):
    assert is_balanced_parens(s) is False


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_input",
    [
        None,
        123,
        3.14,
        object(),
    ],
)
def test_non_iterable_inputs_raise_type_error(bad_input):
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        is_balanced_parens(bad_input)
```

Note: malformed bracket strings are treated as “error cases” returning `False`. The current implementation only raises `TypeError` for non-iterable inputs like `None` or `123`.
